Every dataset used in this textbook is listed below with a one-line description, its source package, and the chapters where it appears. Every dataset is also available as a CSV in this book's [`datasets/`](https://github.com/DataScienceUWL/DataScienceUWL.github.io/tree/main/STAT145/textbook/datasets) folder for use with Jamovi or any other tool.

## From the `openintro` R package {#sec-openintro-data}

These datasets ship with the [openintro R package](https://cran.r-project.org/package=openintro). Install with `install.packages("openintro")` and access via `openintro::name` or `data(name)` after `library(openintro)`. Each name below links to the package's documentation page.

## UWL-local datasets {#sec-local-datasets}

These CSVs are hosted alongside the book and referenced in projects and labs.

| Dataset | Description |
|:--------|:------------|
| [`ai_tool_use.csv`](../datasets/ai_tool_use.csv) | UWL student survey: AI-tool use by age group (small, categorical --- good for two-way tables and inference for two proportions) |
| [`class_survey.csv`](../datasets/class_survey.csv) | UWL student survey: year, housing, study hours, sleep hours, commute (mixed quantitative + categorical --- good for a full EDA project) |
| [`flying_etiquette.csv`](../datasets/flying_etiquette.csv) | FiveThirtyEight survey on in-flight etiquette (many categorical variables --- rich for chi-square practice) |

## Exercise datasets bundled with this book {#sec-ims-exercise-data}

Four CSVs live in `chapters/data/` rather than in an R package, because the
exercises that use them build their figures when the book is rendered. All four
are redistributed **unchanged** from
[*Introduction to Modern Statistics*](https://github.com/OpenIntroStat/ims),
which is licensed CC BY-SA 3.0 --- the same license as this book. The original
data sources are listed so you can go back to them.

| Dataset | Description | Original source | Where used |
|:--------|:------------|:----------------|:-----------|
| `meat.csv` | Meat and carbohydrate consumption vs. life expectancy in 175 countries, averaged over 2011--2013 | @You:2022 | Ch 5, 19 |
| `netflix_titles.csv` | 7,788 Netflix titles with type, rating, production country, and release year | [TidyTuesday, 2021-04-20](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/master/data/2021/2021-04-20), from a [Kaggle dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/shivamb/netflix-shows) | Ch 1 |
| `stanford-open-policing-combined-data.csv` | Traffic-stop summary statistics (stop, search, arrest, and citation rates) by county and driver race | [Stanford Open Policing Project](https://openpolicing.stanford.edu/) [@pierson2020large] | Ch 1 |
| `survey.csv` | GPA and major for students in an introductory statistics course at Duke University | IMS exercise data | Ch 17 |

## Using the datasets

**In Jamovi or another statistics package.** Every dataset above is downloadable as a CSV from the openintro website (e.g., `https://www.openintro.org/data/csv/<name>.csv`), or as tab-separated/txt/rdata from the same page. The UWL-local files are linked directly above.

**In R.** After installing the source package:

```r
library(openintro)
data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")  # if the dataset is in another package
head(mcu_films)                              # peek at the first rows
?mcu_films                                   # open the documentation
```

**Full openintro dataset catalog.** The complete list of openintro datasets (400+, not all used in this book) lives at [openintrostat.github.io/openintro/reference/](https://openintrostat.github.io/openintro/reference/).

::: {.callout-note}
